questions.question_text: $PT$ and $PQ$ are tangents to a circle with centre $O$. The smaller angle $\angle TOQ = 142^{\circ}$. Find $x = \angle TPQ$.

options.why: Copied the central angle instead of calculating $180^{\circ} - 142^{\circ}$.
Halved the central angle, calculating $142^{\circ} \div 2$ instead of using the two tangent-radius right angles.
Calculated $360^{\circ} - 142^{\circ}$ without subtracting the two right angles.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle OTP = \angle OQP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangents meet radii at $90^{\circ}$)
$x + 90^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} + 142^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$ (angle sum of quadrilateral $OTPQ$)
$x = 38^{\circ}$

options.why: Left the answer as $PC^{2}$ instead of taking the square root.
Confused $PQ$ with the chord length $NB$.
Divided $PC^{2} = 100$ by $4$ twice, calculating $100 \div 4 \div 4 = 6.25$, instead of taking its square root.

questions.solution_text:
$PB = PN + NB = 4 + 21 = 25\text{ cm}$
$PC^{2} = PN \times PB$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$PC^{2} = 4 \times 25 = 100$
$PC = 10\text{ cm}$
$PQ = PC$ (tangents from an external point are equal)
$PQ = 10\text{ cm}$

questions.question_text: $PT$ is tangent to a circle with centre $O$ at $T$. Join $OT$, $OP$ and $TP$. Given $\angle TOP = 54^{\circ}$, find $x = \angle OPT$.

options.why: Assumed the two acute angles of $\triangle OTP$ are equal.
Calculated $180^{\circ} - 54^{\circ}$ without subtracting the tangent-radius right angle.
Halved $54^{\circ}$ instead of using the angle sum of the right triangle.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$ (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$x + 90^{\circ} + 54^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle OTP$)
$x = 36^{\circ}$

questions.question_text:
$A$, $B$ and $T$ lie on a circle. The line $XY$ is tangent at $T$, with $X$, $T$ and $Y$ in that order. The triangle lies above $XY$, with $A$ to the left of $B$.
Given $\angle ATB = 47^{\circ}$ and $\angle BTY = 68^{\circ}$, find $c = \angle ABT$.

options.why: Assigned the tangent-chord angle for chord $TB$ to the angle at $B$ instead of the angle at $A$.
Calculated $180^{\circ} - 68^{\circ}$ without subtracting the given triangle angle $47^{\circ}$.
Subtracted the givens, calculating $68^{\circ} - 47^{\circ}$ instead of using the triangle angle sum.

questions.solution_text:
$\angle TAB = 68^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem for chord $TB$)
$c = 180^{\circ} - 47^{\circ} - 68^{\circ} = 65^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle ATB$)

options.why: Left the answer as $PC^{2}$ instead of taking the square root.
Confused $PQ$ with the chord length $NB$.
Divided the full secant length by the external segment, calculating $(2 + 30) \div 2 = 16$, instead of multiplying them and taking the square root.

questions.solution_text:
$PB = PN + NB = 2 + 30 = 32\text{ m}$
$PC^{2} = PN \times PB$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$PC^{2} = 2 \times 32 = 64$
$PC = 8\text{ m}$
$PQ = PC$ (tangents from an external point are equal)
$PQ = 8\text{ m}$

questions.question_text:
$PC$ is tangent to a circle with centre $O$ at $C$. A secant from $P$ meets the circle at $N$ and then $B$.
Given $PN = 25\text{ cm}$, $NB = 24\text{ cm}$ and $OP = 37\text{ cm}$, find (a) $PC$ and (b) the radius $OC$.

options.why: Subtracted lengths, calculating $37 - 35 = 2$, instead of applying Pythagoras' theorem to find the radius.
Reported $OC^{2} = 37^{2} - 35^{2} = 144$ as the radius without taking the square root.
Copied the external secant segment $PN = 25\text{ cm}$ as the tangent length; the tangent length is $35\text{ cm}$.

questions.solution_text:
(a) $PB = PN + NB = 25 + 24 = 49\text{ cm}$
$PC^{2} = PN \times PB$ (square of a tangent equals the product of the intercepts of a secant from the same point)
$PC^{2} = 25 \times 49 = 1225$
$PC = 35\text{ cm}$
(b) $\angle OCP = 90^{\circ}$ (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$37^{2} = OC^{2} + 35^{2}$ (Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle OCP$)
$OC^{2} = 1369 - 1225 = 144$
$OC = 12\text{ cm}$
